simple.meaning: תֹּף (tôph) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a tambourine.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 31:27. The surrounding context includes family, family line, kingship, prophetic witness, city, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תֹּף (H8596) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: תֹּף (tôph) / H8596 is traced through Genesis 31:27, Exodus 15:20, Judges 11:34, 1 Samuel 10:5 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: Why did you flee secretly, and deceive me, and didn’t tell me, that I might have sent you away with mirth and with songs, with tambourine and with harp;
Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a tambourine in her hand; and all the women went out after her with tambourines and with dances.
Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a tambourine in her hand; and all the women went out after her with tambourines and with dances.
Jephthah came to Mizpah to his house; and behold, his daughter came out to meet him with tambourines and with dances. She was his only child. Besides her he had neither son nor daughter.

“After that you will come to the hill of God, where the garrison of the Philistines is; and it will happen, when you have come there to the city, that you will meet a band of prophets coming down from the high place with a lute, a tambourine, a pipe, and a harp before them; and they will be prophesying.

As they came, when David returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, the women came out of all the cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet king Saul, with tambourines, with joy, and with instruments of music.
David and all the house of Israel played before Yahweh with all kinds of instruments made of cypress wood, with harps, with stringed instruments, with tambourines, with castanets, and with cymbals.
David and all Israel played before God with all their might, even with songs, with harps, with stringed instruments, with tambourines, with cymbals, and with trumpets.
They sing to the tambourine and harp,
Blow the trumpet at the New Moon,
Let them praise his name in the dance!
Praise him with tambourine and dancing!
The harp, lyre, tambourine, and flute, with wine, are at their feasts;
The mirth of tambourines ceases. The sound of those who rejoice ends. The joy of the harp ceases.
Every stroke of the rod of punishment, which Yahweh will lay on him, will be with the sound of tambourines and harps. He will fight with them in battles, brandishing weapons.

definitions.full: H8596. toph תֹּף noun masculine timbrel, tambourine ; — absolute ׳ת Gen 31:27 +; plural תֻּמִּים Judg 11:34 +; suffix תֻּמֶּ֫יךָ Ezek 28:13 , תֻּמַּ֫יִח Jer 31:4 ; — timbrel , held and struck with hand, especially by dancing women, often with other musical instruments: — sign of merriment, gladness Gen 31:27 (E) Job 21:12 , reverly Isa 5:12 ; ת ׳מְשׂוֺשׂ 24:8 , compare Jer 31:4 ; Ezek 28:13 ; exultation, triumph Exod 15:20 (twice in verse) (E) Judg 11:34 ; 1Sam 18:6 ; Isa 30:32 ; used by prophets in ecstasy 1Sam 10:5 ; in praise of ׳י 2Sam 6:5 || 1Chr 13:8 ; Psa 81:3 ; 149:3 ; 150:4 . — See Prince EB Music.§ 3 .
